_note: The channel's own recurring creatures (Truman 2026-10-25: original made-up creatures, a recurring cast, awake doing something quiet with breathing and blinks drawn in code). Each is based on a Pacific Northwest animal and has one silly, unrealistic touch the code can animate: a lantern that glows and swings, a scarf blowing in the wind, plants growing on it (never completely realistic). Each 'prompt' is pasted into key-art prompts word for word (tools/new_video.py cast_text) so a creature looks the same in every video: change it only with his OK. 'status': approved (in the cast), candidate (in a lineup, not picked yet), dropped. 'role': the cast slot. One lantern per scene (Truman 2026-10-25: only one holds a lantern; other items, or nothing, look better), held by whoever fits the story; it is a scene prop in the brief, not part of anyone's design (the Burdock Shelter: the salamander, holding its leaf and the lantern, one in each hand, as if searching for something). Lineups: out/style_explore/round3 to round5. 'animates': what the code can bring to life on it besides breathing and blinks. "species": the real Pacific Northwest species each approved character is based on, by its common name; a video's description names them (user 2026-10-26: descriptions name the species). A second troupe ("troupe": "snowy-night", Truman 2026-11-12) belongs to the look pencil-night (colored pencil on black paper): silly, cute friends of the snowy mountains, three real animals with one silly touch each and the made-up yuzu sprite (no species: "based_on" says what it is), picked from the round 8 lineups (out/style_explore/round8).
